title: Add presubmit cost exporter and compact CI prober
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds a lightweight presubmit cost exporter and compact prober to reduce CI spend and improve failure triage. Non-breaking.
description:
Motivation and summary:
This PR introduces two small, linked pieces of work aimed at lowering presubmit CI costs and improving signal for flaky or misconfigured jobs: 1) a presubmit cost exporter that emits per-job time and resource estimates to our telemetry pipeline, and 2) a compact CI prober that runs a thin subset of smoke checks (fast lint + unit-test surface) to give quicker feedback for devs and to exercise release hooks for automation.

What changed (high level):
- New binary: tools/ci/presubmit_cost_exporter (Go) that consumes GitHub Actions job metadata and emits Prometheus metrics via pushgateway and a sidecar for local dev telemetry.
- New compact prober workflow: .github/workflows/compact-prober.yml which runs on push to feature branches and runs in a narrow matrix to quickly validate tooling differences before expensive presubmit runs.
- Staged presubmit lanes: updated .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to add a staged fast-lane that defers heavy integration suites when the compact prober succeeded.
- Small refactor: consolidated lint entrypoints into .github/actions/lint-adapter to avoid per-repo shell drift and reduce image pulls.
- Helper scripts: scripts/update-deps.sh to automate dep bump PR creation using the new cost exporter heuristics (skips large updates during high-cost windows).
- Docs: docs/dev/ci.md updated with guidance for running the prober locally, interpreting cost metrics, and how to opt out for WIP PRs.

Checklist (implemented):
- [x] Add presubmit_cost_exporter with config for pushgateway and local dry-run
- [x] Create compact-prober workflow and schedule to run on pushes
- [x] Wire fast-lane gating in presubmit.yml (defer heavy integration when prober passes)
- [x] Consolidate lint entrypoint action and migrate workspace scripts
- [x] Add docs and examples for devs
- [x] Add automation to skip dependency bumps during peak CI windows

Commits (summary):
- Add presubmit cost exporter and metric names, config and tests
- Add compact-prober workflow and matrix definition
- Refactor lint adapter into composite action and update usages
- Hook fast-lane gating into presubmit workflow
- Add update-deps script and ci heuristics
- Docs: CI troubleshooting and local prober runbook

Files changed (representative):
- tools/ci/presubmit_cost_exporter/main.go (+410 LOC added, simple HTTP server, Prom client, tests)
- .github/workflows/compact-prober.yml (new, 72 lines)
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (modified: added fast-lane gating and cost annotations)
- .github/actions/lint-adapter/action.yml (new composite action, 60 lines)
- scripts/update-deps.sh (new helper for automated dep bumps)
- docs/dev/ci.md (edited, +28 lines)
- Makefile (small target to run prober locally)
- ci/fastpath-config.yaml (new config with thresholds for skipping heavy lanes)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Liam O'Connor: "Can you justify the choice of pushgateway vs direct scrape? We need to ensure we don't increase cardinality in prod metrics."
- Priya (author): "Pushgateway choice is deliberate to make it easy for ephemeral GitHub Actions runners to push and for our telemetry pipeline to ingest without instrumenting each runner. We scope metric labels to job_kind and repo only to limit cardinality. Added tests asserting label set length."
- Ava Chen: "The compact-prober matrix looks good, but we should ensure the prober uses the same lint config as presubmit to avoid false positives."
- Priya: "Updated the prober to mount the canonical lint config from .github/ and added an assertion step that the config hash matches main's config for the repo."
- Diego Morales: "update-deps script feels powerful; can it accidentally open huge bump PRs during high-traffic hours?"
- Priya: "Added a CI heuristic file (ci/fastpath-config.yaml) and a guard in update-deps.sh that exits early if the exporter signals high-cost window. Also introduced a dry-run flag for staging."
- Liam O'Connor: "Please add a small e2e test that validates the gating behavior so we don't regress when changing presubmit lanes."
- Priya: "Added a unit test for gating logic and a smoke e2e in tools/ci tests."

CI results and iterations:
- Initial run: compact-prober failed due to lint action path mismatch (expected ./.github/actions/lint-adapter). Fixed action name and repushed.
- Second run: two flaky unit tests caught; author fixed a race in in-memory cache used by presubmit_cost_exporter tests.
- Third run: all checks passed (unit, lint composite, compact-prober, presubmit gating smoke).

Rationale and impact:
- Expected CI cost savings: migrating quick-failure checks into compact-prober and gating heavy suites reduces average presubmit runner-hours by ~18% in a two-week pilot (measured with presubmit_cost_exporter).
- Developer experience: faster feedback loop for most trivial failures; docs and Makefile target make local runs easier for contributors.
- Release automation: the compact prober runs the same release-hook smoke checks so automation is less likely to regress between endorsing changes and running full release flows.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- No runtime or API changes to production services. All change is CI/build tooling.
- update-deps.sh defaults to dry-run and requires an explicit --apply flag and service token; automation only opens PRs when the exporter indicates a non-peak window.

Follow-ups and known limitations:
- Extend exporter to include per-job cost attribution for cached vs cold runs (next sprint).
- Add Grafana dashboard tiles and an alert for sustained cost spikes (tracked in ENG-2440).
- Evaluate replacing pushgateway with a short-lived pull endpoint if cardinality concerns grow.

Merge notes:
- Squash-merged after approvals from Liam and Ava. Changelog entry added under "Infra / CI". No migration steps required for downstream consumers.

If you want to run locally:
- make prober-run  # builds compact prober image and runs checks against current branch
- tools/ci/presubmit_cost_exporter --dry-run --pushgateway=http://localhost:9091

If anything looks off I can follow up with a hotfix; I avoided any sweeping cross-repo changes and kept the lint adapter narrowly scoped to prevent accidental breakage.
